newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government bonds end higher across board.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government bonds end higher across board.

text.p: Singapore government bonds ended higher across the board in moderate trade on interbank and retail interest, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Bonds prices were marked up slightly today following a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bills were slightly lower. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.23/1.18 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.50/1.45 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.70/1.65 percent against 1.82/1.77 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.73/98.78 from Monday's close of S$98.63/98.68, September 2001 at S$97.35/97.40 versus S$97.20/97.25 and June 2003 at S$95.35/95.40 against S$95.20/95.25.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-7/8 2-3/4 percent from Monday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
